subject: Recap: multi-customer QoS, per-customer routing & quota needs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@nimbus.health>, Alex Carter <alex@cloudops.io>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbus.health>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: multi-customer QoS, per-customer routing & quota needs

Hi Sam / Alex —

Thanks for the call this morning — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on Nimbus's high-level goals. Short recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I pulled these notes from the discovery with Laura and Marissa on the call.

Pain points and drivers
- Noisy tenants are causing tail-latency spikes for a small set of customers (particularly during overnight batch jobs).
- You need per-customer spend caps and quota enforcement to avoid surprise bills from model usage.
- Certain customers require isolated performance (Gold) and must be routed to dedicated capacity or a higher-priority queue.
- Auditability & compliance (HIPAA scope for PII, detailed request logs, and per-tenant data isolation) are hard to prove with your current provider.

Current stack / constraints you mentioned
- Front-end request routing is homegrown; model calls go to a mix of OpenEndpoint-managed endpoints and a self-hosted inference layer.
- Daily request volume today ~ 150k LLM requests/day with 3x expected growth over 12 months.
- Procurement lead time ~ 4 weeks for any new vendor contract / PO.

Success criteria (what success looks like for Nimbus)
- P95 generation latency < 150ms for Gold-tier customers at steady state.
- Per-customer monthly spend caps and automatic throttling once hit.
- Ability to pin customers to dedicated GPU pools (or equivalent isolated routing) with clear failover to shared capacity.
- End-to-end audit logs, SOC2 evidence, and options for a private deployment (VPC) if needed.

Proposed next steps / MAP (attached: nimbus-map-draft.pdf)
1) Redwood to share a short Mutual Action Plan and a sample QoS config (attached). -- owner: Karthik (today)
2) Schedule an engineering deep dive on routing + KV cache isolation (Laura to lead). -- owner: Laura (next week)
3) Procurement review & preliminary SOW + ballpark pricing for a 3-week pilot dedicated pool. -- owner: Procurement / Karthik (w/in 48h)
4) Security questionnaire kickoff (Redwood security + Nimbus security). -- owner: Security teams (schedule pending)

Open questions from our side
- Would you prefer a hard per-customer token cap (reject) or soft throttling (queue/backpressure) after the cap?
- Are there regulated tenants that require an on-prem or VPC-only deployment immediately, or is a hosted + dedicated pool acceptable as a first step?

I attached a brief MAP and a sample QoS config for your review (nimbus-map-draft.pdf, qos-sample-config.yaml). I can be on a call tomorrow afternoon for any follow-ups.

Thanks again — looking forward to the next steps.

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Sam Green <sam.green@nimbus.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Carter <alex@cloudops.io>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbus.health>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: multi-customer QoS, per-customer routing & quota needs

Thanks Karthik — that's a great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume: current peak is closer to 10k RPS for inference during daytime windows across all customers; daily number you cited aligns with our totals. Expect traffic to grow as we add two new partners in Q1.
- Isolation: Gold customers must not experience >10% latency degradation when noisy tenants spike.
- Billing: procurement will want a predictable monthly committed amount for Dedicated + an overage rate. Can you provide a committed capacity tier (e.g., 2x, 4x GPU pool sizing) and a very rough monthly estimate so we can fast-track budgeting?
- Compliance: HIPAA is a hard requirement for a subset of our customers; we'll need the SOC2/BAA conversation early.

Procurement (cc'd) — can you confirm the PO cadence and any required vendor documents?

Happy to take the MAP and QoS sample and route internally. Also happy to schedule the engineering deep dive next Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Date: 2026-11-15T16:00:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Recap: multi-customer QoS, per-customer routing & quota needs — ballpark & pilot plan

Sam / team —

Quick follow-up with ballpark numbers for budgeting purposes and an ask to lock a deep-dive slot. These are very high-level estimates for a 3-week pilot focused on routing + per-customer isolation:

- Dedicated small pool (2x A100-equivalent): ~$28k/month committed.
- Dedicated medium pool (4x A100-equivalent): ~$52k/month committed.
- Overages billed at usage rate + 30% premium; we can formalize in SOW.

Attached: qos-sample-config.yaml (example of per-customer QoS rules and token caps). I also attached the draft MAP (nimbus-map-draft.pdf) that outlines milestones and acceptance criteria.

Next steps / calendar
- Laura to run the engineering deep dive: Tue 2026-11-17 11:00-12:00 PT or Wed 2026-11-18 14:00-15:00 PT. Please confirm preferred slot.
- Procurement: if you share the vendor checklist we’ll prepare the requested documents (SOC2 report, BAA template, network diagram).

Action items
- Karthik: finalize MAP and send official ballpark proposal (today).
- Laura: prep deep-dive agenda and sample routing tests (by EOD Mon).
- Procurement: confirm timeline for PO (Procurement) and any required forms.

Let me know which deep-dive slot works and we'll send calendar invites.

Thanks,
--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: qos-sample-config.yaml (text), nimbus-map-draft.pdf (1 page PDF)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Recap: multi-customer QoS, per-customer routing & quota needs — internal prep

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks — looping in a few quick internal notes:
- I'll draft the deep-dive agenda with three focused sections: routing architecture, cache isolation tests, and acceptance criteria for P95/throughput.
- I'll ask SRE to provision a small test pool we can use for simulated noisy-tenant runs. If we need a VPC demo, we'll scope that separately.
- I'll prep a short runbook for per-customer cap behavior (hard reject vs throttling) and bring recommended defaults.

I'll share the agenda by EOD Monday and will be on the call Tue/Wed.

Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
